questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: A retail site expects credential stuffing against its login endpoint during a sale. Which edge strategy should the security architect select?

answers.text: Use AWS WAF rate-based and bot-control protections at CloudFront with authentication failure monitoring
Increase the origin database storage class only
Use VPC network ACLs as the only login protection
Disable access logging during the sale

explanations.a: Credential stuffing is a layer 7 abuse pattern, so edge filtering and rate controls near CloudFront can reduce malicious login attempts before they reach the origin.
explanations.b: Database storage class changes do not reduce credential stuffing at the edge.
explanations.c: Network ACLs do not inspect HTTP login behavior or credential stuffing patterns.
explanations.d: Removing edge and application logs would reduce detection of login abuse.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: An API is targeted by SQL injection and path traversal probes. Which edge security strategy aligns with the anticipated attack?

answers.text: Use only Shield Advanced without any web-layer rules
Apply AWS WAF managed rule groups for common web exploits and tune exceptions with logs
Rely only on security groups for query-string inspection
Move all application logs into a private subnet

explanations.a: Shield Advanced helps with DDoS events but does not replace HTTP exploit inspection.
explanations.b: Managed web exploit rules can block OWASP-style attacks while logs support safe tuning for legitimate traffic.
explanations.c: Security groups filter ports and IPs and cannot inspect web request parameters.
explanations.d: Log location alone does not block SQL injection or path traversal probes.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: A media company expects volumetric HTTP floods against a public origin. Which edge strategy provides the strongest first line of defense?

answers.text: Expose the origin directly and scale only the database
Use IAM permission boundaries to filter HTTP floods
Front the origin with CloudFront, AWS WAF, and Shield Advanced protections
Disable all caching to force requests to the origin

explanations.a: Direct origin exposure increases attack surface and database scaling does not absorb edge floods.
explanations.b: Permission boundaries constrain IAM identities and do not process viewer traffic.
explanations.c: CloudFront and AWS WAF reduce origin exposure, while Shield Advanced adds DDoS response capabilities for protected resources.
explanations.d: Forcing all requests to the origin can increase impact during floods.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: A company hosts public static content in S3 and wants controlled browser access from a specific application domain. Which threat should guide the edge strategy?

answers.text: EC2 instance metadata abuse from the browser
KMS grant sprawl on unrelated databases
Patch drift on container hosts
Misconfigured CORS allowing unintended origins to access objects

explanations.a: Browser CORS for S3 does not control EC2 metadata access.
explanations.b: KMS grants are not the browser-origin control for public static content.
explanations.c: Host patch drift does not define the S3 CORS strategy.
explanations.d: S3 CORS controls browser cross-origin behavior, so the strategy must limit origins and methods to the intended application.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: A globally distributed API must block requests from embargoed countries and known malicious IP ranges. Which edge strategy fits?

answers.text: Use CloudFront geographic restrictions and AWS WAF IP sets with logging
Use only a private subnet route table on the origin
Use only Lambda execution role permissions
Use only EBS encryption on origin instances

explanations.a: Geographic and IP-based edge controls can enforce location and source restrictions before requests reach the application.
explanations.b: Origin routing does not stop unwanted public viewers at the edge.
explanations.c: Execution roles authorize Lambda AWS API calls and do not filter viewer countries or IP ranges.
explanations.d: Storage encryption does not restrict request source geography or IP reputation.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: An IoT platform needs to prevent devices with invalid policies from publishing to sensitive topics. Which edge-adjacent strategy applies?

answers.text: Use CloudFront cache behaviors for MQTT authorization
Use AWS IoT policies that scope device principals to approved MQTT topics and actions
Use S3 Object Lock on device messages as the only control
Use network ACLs to inspect MQTT topic names

explanations.a: CloudFront cache behavior does not authorize AWS IoT Core MQTT topics.
explanations.b: AWS IoT policies authorize device communication at the IoT service edge and limit topic access.
explanations.c: Object retention does not authorize device publish and subscribe actions.
explanations.d: Network ACLs do not parse and authorize MQTT topic names.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.1: Define and select edge security strategies based on anticipated threats and attacks.
questions.text: A public API uses third-party clients with highly variable request rates. The team needs protection without blocking legitimate bursts from trusted partners. Which strategy should be selected?

answers.text: Set one very low global rate limit for all clients
Remove WAF protections to avoid false positives
Combine AWS WAF rate limiting, partner-specific allow rules, and monitoring to tune thresholds
Move the API to a single private EC2 instance with no edge controls

explanations.a: A single low limit can block legitimate partner traffic during normal bursts.
explanations.b: Removing web protections exposes the API to the anticipated abuse.
explanations.c: A blended edge strategy can limit abusive rates while making explicit allowance for known trusted client patterns.
explanations.d: A single unprotected origin weakens public API security and availability.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution fronts a public ALB. The application must reduce clickjacking and content-sniffing risks. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Add an inbound security group rule for every browser
Store headers in Secrets Manager
Enable S3 Versioning on an unrelated bucket
Add security response headers through CloudFront response headers policies

explanations.a: Security groups do not set browser security headers.
explanations.b: Secrets Manager stores sensitive values and does not inject response headers.
explanations.c: S3 Versioning does not reduce browser clickjacking or content sniffing.
explanations.d: CloudFront response headers policies can add browser security headers close to viewers without changing each origin.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: A public API requires protection against OWASP Top 10 attacks. Which edge protection is appropriate?

answers.text: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with managed rule groups to the API entry point
Use only an EC2 instance profile on the origin
Use only VPC Flow Logs
Use only a KMS key policy

explanations.a: AWS WAF managed rule groups can inspect web requests for common application-layer attack patterns.
explanations.b: Instance profiles authorize AWS API calls and do not inspect HTTP requests.
explanations.c: Flow logs record network metadata but do not block OWASP request payloads.
explanations.d: KMS policies protect key use and do not filter web requests.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: An S3-backed web application allows browser uploads only from https://app.example.com. Which protection should be configured?

answers.text: Wildcard CORS origins and methods for ease of integration
Restrictive S3 CORS rules for the approved origin, methods, and headers
A security group attached to the S3 bucket
A Lambda execution role with no bucket policy review

explanations.a: Wildcard browser access can allow unintended origins to interact with the bucket.
explanations.b: CORS rules should allow only the required browser origin and operations for the application.
explanations.c: S3 buckets do not use security groups.
explanations.d: Lambda role permissions do not define browser CORS behavior.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: A company is experiencing application-layer DDoS against CloudFront paths. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Increase RDS backup retention only
Use network ACLs on private subnets as the only edge control
AWS WAF rate-based rules and Shield Advanced protections for the distribution
Disable CloudFront logging and rely on user reports

explanations.a: Backup retention does not mitigate active layer 7 request floods.
explanations.b: Private subnet network ACLs do not inspect requests before CloudFront or the ALB.
explanations.c: Rate-based WAF rules can limit abusive HTTP request rates, and Shield Advanced adds DDoS support for protected edge resources.
explanations.d: Logging supports tuning and investigation during attacks.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: An IoT device should publish only to its own topic namespace. Which edge protection should be implemented?

answers.text: AWS WAF SQL injection rules for MQTT topics
A public S3 bucket policy for device certificates
CloudFront geo restriction for device identity
AWS IoT policy using thing or certificate attributes to limit publish and subscribe topics

explanations.a: WAF web rules do not authorize MQTT topic access in AWS IoT Core.
explanations.b: Public certificate storage is unsafe and does not authorize MQTT actions.
explanations.c: Geographic restrictions do not establish per-device MQTT authorization.
explanations.d: Scoped IoT policies restrict device principals to the topic paths they are allowed to use.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: A public origin should receive traffic only from CloudFront, not directly from the internet. Which implementation helps?

answers.text: Restrict the origin using security groups or policies that allow CloudFront-origin traffic patterns where supported
Publish the origin DNS name in client applications
Allow 0.0.0.0/0 to the origin on every administrative and application port
Use only application log retention to protect the origin

explanations.a: Origin protection reduces bypass of CloudFront and AWS WAF by limiting direct access to the origin.
explanations.b: Direct origin exposure encourages bypass of edge controls.
explanations.c: Broad internet access weakens origin protection.
explanations.d: Log retention does not prevent direct origin access.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.2: Implement appropriate network edge protection.
questions.text: A business wants web request blocking managed centrally across many accounts. Which service can help deploy AWS WAF policies at scale?

answers.text: Amazon EFS Lifecycle Management
AWS Firewall Manager
AWS CodeArtifact domains
Amazon SQS visibility timeout

explanations.a: EFS lifecycle policies manage file storage classes and not WAF deployment.
explanations.b: Firewall Manager can centrally manage AWS WAF policies across accounts in AWS Organizations.
explanations.c: CodeArtifact manages software packages and not web ACL policy enforcement.
explanations.d: Visibility timeout controls message processing and not edge web protection.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: A web application must block requests from specific countries while allowing global static content delivery. Which edge rule design is appropriate?

answers.text: Block countries with an IAM permissions boundary
Use only database row-level security
Use CloudFront geographic restrictions or AWS WAF geographic match rules for the protected application paths
Move the protected paths to a public origin with no WAF

explanations.a: Permissions boundaries apply to IAM identities and do not filter viewer geography.
explanations.b: Database rules do not block viewer requests at the edge.
explanations.c: Geographic controls can enforce location-based requirements while allowing other distribution behavior to remain global.
explanations.d: Removing edge controls undermines the geographic requirement.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: An API must slow abusive clients that exceed 1,000 requests in five minutes. Which AWS edge rule should be used?

answers.text: S3 Lifecycle expiration rule
KMS automatic rotation
EC2 user data script
AWS WAF rate-based rule

explanations.a: Object lifecycle settings do not throttle HTTP clients.
explanations.b: Key rotation does not rate-limit API callers.
explanations.c: User data runs on instance launch and does not enforce edge rate limits.
explanations.d: Rate-based rules track request volume by aggregation key and can block or count clients that exceed thresholds.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: A fraud team wants to challenge clients with suspicious browser fingerprints while allowing known mobile apps. Which edge design fits?

answers.text: Use AWS WAF rules that combine managed bot signals, custom headers, and explicit app allow conditions
Apply one unconditional CAPTCHA to every API call
Use only subnet route tables to identify browsers
Disable all headers before WAF inspection

explanations.a: Client fingerprinting and known-client conditions can distinguish suspicious browser traffic from trusted app behavior.
explanations.b: Unconditional challenges can break legitimate mobile app and API clients.
explanations.c: Route tables do not evaluate browser or client fingerprint signals.
explanations.d: Headers often provide important context for client identification and rule logic.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: An application requires different WAF rules for /login and /public paths. What design should be used?

answers.text: Apply only a single origin security group rule for every URI
Create path-aware AWS WAF rules or separate behaviors that apply protections according to request URI
Use only one S3 CORS rule for login throttling
Require database encryption to distinguish URI paths

explanations.a: Security groups cannot evaluate HTTP paths.
explanations.b: Path-aware edge logic lets sensitive endpoints receive stricter controls without overblocking low-risk paths.
explanations.c: CORS does not provide login request rate limiting.
explanations.d: Database encryption does not drive edge path decisions.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: A company needs to allow partner traffic only when requests include a signed header and originate from an approved IP range. Which edge rule design fits?

answers.text: Allow all traffic from the internet if the path starts with /partner
Use an EC2 key pair name as the request authentication control
AWS WAF rule logic that combines header matching and IP set conditions
Rely on CloudWatch dashboard annotations for enforcement

explanations.a: Path alone does not verify partner identity or source.
explanations.b: EC2 key pair names do not validate HTTP requests.
explanations.c: Combining multiple WAF conditions enforces both source and request property requirements.
explanations.d: Annotations do not block or allow requests.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: A distribution should redirect HTTP viewers to HTTPS and apply modern TLS settings. Which edge configuration is required?

answers.text: EBS encryption on origin volumes only
A DynamoDB table encryption key
An SQS delay queue for all requests
CloudFront viewer protocol policy and security policy settings

explanations.a: Origin disk encryption does not enforce viewer HTTPS.
explanations.b: DynamoDB encryption does not control CloudFront viewer protocol.
explanations.c: SQS delay queues do not configure CloudFront TLS behavior.
explanations.d: Viewer protocol and TLS policy settings enforce secure viewer connections at the distribution edge.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.3: Design and implement AWS edge controls and rules based on requirements.
questions.text: A security team must test new AWS WAF rules without immediately blocking production users. What rule action should be used first?

answers.text: Count mode with log review before switching to block
Delete all logs before enabling the rule
Set block action on every request regardless of pattern
Bypass the web ACL for production paths

explanations.a: Count mode lets teams observe matches and tune rule logic before enforcing blocking behavior.
explanations.b: This approach logs are needed to evaluate false positives and attack matches.
explanations.c: Unconditional blocking can create an outage.
explanations.d: Bypassing the web ACL prevents testing the intended production traffic patterns.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A company subscribes to a managed third-party WAF rule set for AWS WAF. What integration consideration matters most?

answers.text: Assume third-party rules never need tuning
Test third-party rules in count mode and monitor false positives before enforcement
Disable all AWS managed rules when adding any third-party rule
Give the third-party provider root access to all accounts

explanations.a: External rules can still produce false positives for specific applications.
explanations.b: Third-party rules can add coverage, but production enforcement should be tuned against real application traffic.
explanations.c: AWS managed and third-party rules can be layered when priorities are designed carefully.
explanations.d: Rule subscription does not require sharing root credentials.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A security data lake ingests CloudFront and WAF logs in OCSF-compatible format for a partner SIEM. What should be preserved?

answers.text: Only the compressed object size
Only the name of the analyst who created the lake
Source service, account, Region, request metadata, action, rule ID, and event time
No timestamps because the SIEM can guess ordering

explanations.a: Object size does not preserve request or rule context.
explanations.b: Analyst identity does not describe the edge event.
explanations.c: OCSF-aligned integration remains useful only when core fields needed for correlation and triage are retained.
explanations.d: Timestamps are essential for incident timelines and correlation.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A company uses a third-party CDN in front of AWS origins and wants AWS WAF to evaluate traffic at the origin ALB. What integration issue must be addressed?

answers.text: Removing all forwarding headers before the ALB
Allowing the internet to bypass the CDN and ALB protections
Using only database encryption to identify client IPs
Preserving trusted client IP information and preventing direct origin bypass

explanations.a: Removing client context can make rate and source-based rules less useful.
explanations.b: Direct origin access can evade intended third-party and AWS controls.
explanations.c: Database encryption does not preserve edge client identity.
explanations.d: Third-party edge integration requires reliable source identity and origin protection so rules evaluate meaningful traffic context.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A third-party security tool needs near-real-time AWS WAF logs. Which AWS integration pattern is appropriate?

answers.text: Deliver WAF logs to a supported stream or storage destination that the tool can consume with least-privilege access
Email raw logs manually at the end of the month
Give the tool the management account root password
Write logs into an EC2 instance store volume only

explanations.a: WAF log integrations should use supported delivery destinations and scoped access for external consumers.
explanations.b: Monthly manual transfer is too slow and hard to govern.
explanations.c: Root sharing is excessive and unsafe for log consumption.
explanations.d: Instance store is not durable or scalable for security log integration.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution uses Lambda@Edge for request processing. What integration risk should be reviewed?

answers.text: Whether the edge function can train machine learning models
Whether edge code handles security headers, redirects, and input safely without leaking sensitive data
Whether S3 lifecycle rules use the same prefix
Whether the distribution has a decorative comment

explanations.a: Model training is not the core edge security integration concern.
explanations.b: Edge code can affect request and response security and must be reviewed like other security-sensitive code.
explanations.c: Lifecycle prefixes do not validate edge code behavior.
explanations.d: Comments do not reduce edge code security risk.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A WAF rule set should be deployed consistently across accounts and integrated with logging. Which service helps centrally manage this?

answers.text: AWS Backup Vault Lock
Amazon Cognito user pool groups
AWS Firewall Manager with centralized logging destinations
Amazon EFS mount targets

explanations.a: Vault Lock protects backups and does not distribute WAF policies.
explanations.b: Cognito groups authorize application users and do not deploy WAF web ACLs.
explanations.c: Firewall Manager can deploy WAF policies across accounts while logging destinations support central analysis.
explanations.d: Mount targets provide file-system access and not edge security policy management.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.1.4: Configure integrations with AWS edge services and third-party services.
questions.text: A partner requires API access to edge security logs. What access model should be used?

answers.text: Public read access on the entire log archive
Shared administrator keys stored in the partner portal
A security group rule that grants S3 read access
Cross-account or external role access scoped to the required log prefixes and read operations

explanations.a: Public logs can expose sensitive request and security details.
explanations.b: Long-term shared administrator keys create unnecessary risk.
explanations.c: Security groups do not authorize S3 object reads.
explanations.d: Scoped role access limits the partner to the log data needed for integration and preserves auditability.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A company builds EC2 AMIs for production web servers. Which practice best hardens the image before deployment?

answers.text: Use EC2 Image Builder to apply baseline configuration, remove unnecessary packages, run tests, and publish approved AMIs
Patch instances manually after launch with no image updates
Bake administrator access keys into the AMI
Use the oldest available community AMI to preserve compatibility

explanations.a: A hardened AMI pipeline makes security configuration repeatable and validates the image before it reaches production.
explanations.b: Manual post-launch changes create drift and slow vulnerability remediation.
explanations.c: Embedded keys expose long-term credentials to every instance created from the image.
explanations.d: Unvetted old images can contain vulnerabilities and unsupported software.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A container image should not run as root and should contain only runtime dependencies. What build control supports this?

answers.text: Install every debugging package in production images
Use a minimal base image, nonroot user, dependency pinning, and image scanning in the build pipeline
Use the root user for every process to avoid permission issues
Disable image scanning to speed deployment

explanations.a: Extra packages increase attack surface and vulnerability count.
explanations.b: Reducing image contents and privileges limits attack surface and scanning validates known vulnerabilities.
explanations.c: Root execution increases impact if the container is compromised.
explanations.d: Skipping scanning removes a key validation point for hardened images.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: An AMI pipeline must prove that a security agent is installed and running before image distribution. What should be added?

answers.text: An AMI name that includes the word secure
A manual note in the release ticket only
Image validation tests that verify agent installation, configuration, and service status
Delayed testing after the AMI is already used in production

explanations.a: Image naming does not prove security controls are installed.
explanations.b: A note does not validate the built image.
explanations.c: Hardened image pipelines need tests that confirm required controls are actually present and functional.
explanations.d: Late testing can allow noncompliant images into workloads.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A team uses multiple base images from public registries. What supply chain control should be implemented?

answers.text: Always pull the latest tag during production deployment
Trust any public image if it has many downloads
Remove vulnerability scanning from the pipeline
Use trusted base images, verify image provenance, scan vulnerabilities, and pin versions or digests

explanations.a: Mutable latest tags can change without review and weaken reproducibility.
explanations.b: Popularity is not a security validation method.
explanations.c: Scanning helps detect known issues before deployment.
explanations.d: Container supply chain hardening depends on trusted sources and repeatable references to known image content.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A hardened EC2 image includes application secrets for convenience. What should be changed?

answers.text: Remove secrets from the image and retrieve them at runtime from a managed secret store
Encrypt the AMI name only
Copy the same secret into every golden image
Store secrets in shell history on first boot

explanations.a: Images should be reusable artifacts without embedded secrets that spread across every instance.
explanations.b: AMI names are metadata and do not protect embedded secrets.
explanations.c: Image-baked secrets increase exposure and complicate rotation.
explanations.d: Shell history can expose credentials and is not a secret management system.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A security baseline requires CIS-style host hardening for Linux EC2 workloads. Which approach is maintainable?

answers.text: Ask administrators to harden servers manually during incidents
Codify baseline controls in the image build and configuration management process
Keep the baseline only in a slide deck
Apply hardening only to instances that have already been compromised

explanations.a: Manual emergency hardening is inconsistent and late.
explanations.b: Automated baseline enforcement makes hardened host configuration repeatable and auditable.
explanations.c: Documentation alone does not apply controls to hosts.
explanations.d: Security controls should exist before compromise.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.1: Design and implement hardened Amazon EC2 AMIs and container images to secure compute workloads and embed security controls.
questions.keyword: Hardened AMI and container image design
questions.text: A container image was approved last month, but new CVEs were published. What image lifecycle control is needed?

answers.text: Assume approved images remain secure forever
Delete all image metadata to reduce noise
Continuous rescanning and rebuilds of approved images when relevant vulnerabilities appear
Ignore running images and scan only source code comments

explanations.a: Previously approved images can become vulnerable as new CVEs are disclosed.
explanations.b: Metadata is needed to determine which workloads use affected images.
explanations.c: Image hardening is an ongoing process because vulnerabilities can be discovered after initial approval.
explanations.d: Runtime artifacts must be mapped to vulnerability data.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: An EC2 application needs read access to one S3 bucket. Which authorization model should be used?

answers.text: Store an administrator access key in the application configuration
Attach an IAM group directly to the instance
Use a security group rule to grant S3 permissions
Attach an instance profile with an IAM role scoped to the required S3 actions and bucket resources

explanations.a: Long-term administrator keys create unnecessary blast radius.
explanations.b: IAM groups are for users and cannot be attached to EC2 instances.
explanations.c: Security groups control network traffic and do not authorize S3 APIs.
explanations.d: Instance profiles provide temporary credentials to EC2 and avoid hardcoded keys while supporting least privilege.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: An ECS task must write to DynamoDB but should not inherit the EC2 container instance role. What should be configured?

answers.text: An ECS task role with the DynamoDB permissions required by the task
Use the container instance role for all tasks
Put DynamoDB keys into the container image
Use a load balancer listener rule as the task identity

explanations.a: Task roles provide per-task AWS credentials and avoid sharing host-level permissions with every container.
explanations.b: The instance role can overgrant unrelated tasks on the host.
explanations.c: Embedded keys are long-term secrets and hard to rotate.
explanations.d: Listener rules do not authorize AWS API calls.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: A Lambda function needs to decrypt one KMS-encrypted secret and write logs. Which role should be configured?

answers.text: A human IAM Identity Center permission set attached to the function
A Lambda execution role with kms:Decrypt for the specific key and CloudWatch Logs permissions
A shared root access key in environment variables
An S3 bucket ACL on the deployment package

explanations.a: Workforce permission sets do not serve as Lambda execution roles.
explanations.b: The execution role is the function identity and should contain only the actions and resources the function requires.
explanations.c: Root credentials are excessive and unsafe for Lambda execution.
explanations.d: Deployment package ACLs do not grant runtime KMS or logging access.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: An EKS pod needs AWS API access separate from other pods on the same nodes. What should be used?

answers.text: Give every pod the node instance profile
Store one access key in a Kubernetes ConfigMap
IAM roles for service accounts
Use a Kubernetes label as the only AWS authorization control

explanations.a: Node-wide credentials overgrant workloads and weaken isolation.
explanations.b: ConfigMaps are not a secure store for static AWS credentials.
explanations.c: IAM roles for service accounts map pod identity to scoped AWS permissions without sharing the node role.
explanations.d: Labels alone do not authorize AWS API calls.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: A CodeBuild project deploys infrastructure. What compute workload role design is appropriate?

answers.text: Use the developer's personal access key in the buildspec
Give the build project root credentials for all accounts
Remove all IAM permissions and expect deployment to work
A CodeBuild service role with scoped permissions or a role assumption path into target accounts

explanations.a: Personal keys in buildspec files create exposure and accountability problems.
explanations.b: Root credentials are excessive and should not be used by build workloads.
explanations.c: AWS API deployment requires an authorized role.
explanations.d: Build services should use temporary service roles with the minimum deployment permissions needed.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: A Step Functions state machine invokes Lambda and starts ECS tasks. Which roles must be distinguished?

answers.text: The Step Functions execution role and the service roles used by invoked compute services
Use one unrestricted administrator role for every service forever
Use IAM users as state machine states
Use network ACLs to grant Lambda invocation rights

explanations.a: Each service needs the permissions required for its own actions, and confused role boundaries can cause overpermission or failure.
explanations.b: A single broad role increases blast radius and hides service-specific needs.
explanations.c: IAM users do not model workflow states or service execution identity.
explanations.d: Network ACLs do not authorize service API calls.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.2: Apply instance profiles, service roles, and execution roles appropriately to authorize compute workloads.
questions.text: A compute workload cannot assume a cross-account role. What should be checked first?

answers.text: Only the workload's CPU reservation
The source role permissions, target role trust policy, external ID or conditions, and session policy constraints
Only the subnet route to an internet gateway
Only the image tag name

explanations.a: CPU reservation does not control STS authorization.
explanations.b: Cross-account role assumption requires both caller permission and a trust policy that allows the specific principal and conditions.
explanations.c: Network reachability can matter for API calls, but trust and permission policies determine authorization.
explanations.d: Image tags do not grant role assumption rights.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A security team wants to scan ECR container images for known vulnerabilities and send findings to Security Hub. Which service should be used?

answers.text: AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon Route 53 Resolver
Amazon Inspector enhanced scanning
AWS DataSync

explanations.a: ACM manages certificates and does not scan container image packages.
explanations.b: Resolver handles DNS and does not assess container vulnerabilities.
explanations.c: Inspector can scan container images and integrate findings with AWS security workflows.
explanations.d: DataSync transfers data and does not scan images.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A Lambda application uses vulnerable dependencies. Which scanning capability can identify the issue?

answers.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration
VPC Reachability Analyzer only
CloudFront cache invalidation
Amazon Inspector scanning for Lambda functions where supported

explanations.a: Transfer Acceleration improves uploads and does not scan Lambda dependencies.
explanations.b: Reachability analysis does not inspect function package vulnerabilities.
explanations.c: Cache invalidation does not assess software packages.
explanations.d: Inspector can assess supported Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A runtime finding shows an EC2 instance querying a known malicious domain. Which service is likely to produce this threat finding?

answers.text: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Backup
AWS CodeArtifact
Amazon Cognito hosted UI

explanations.a: GuardDuty analyzes DNS and other signals to detect suspicious behavior such as malicious domain communication.
explanations.b: Backup manages recovery points and does not detect malicious DNS activity.
explanations.c: CodeArtifact stores packages and does not monitor EC2 runtime behavior.
explanations.d: Cognito hosted UI authenticates users and does not detect EC2 DNS threats.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A vulnerability finding references an image digest. What should the security engineer do to assess exposure?

answers.text: Assume every image in ECR is running in production
Map the digest to running tasks, deployments, and repositories before prioritizing remediation
Delete all images without checking deployments
Ignore the digest and use tag names only

explanations.a: Repository images are not always deployed.
explanations.b: Image digest mapping shows whether the vulnerable artifact is actually deployed and where it runs.
explanations.c: Unreviewed deletion can break workloads and still leave running tasks unchanged.
explanations.d: Tags can be mutable, while digests identify image content.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A team wants vulnerability scans to fail a build when critical issues are found. What pipeline behavior is appropriate?

answers.text: Scan only after production deployment and never alert
Allow critical vulnerabilities when the build is fast
Run security scans before promotion and gate releases on policy thresholds
Replace scanning with a manual comment that security was considered

explanations.a: Late silent scanning cannot prevent vulnerable releases.
explanations.b: Build speed does not reduce vulnerability risk.
explanations.c: Pre-deployment scanning with clear thresholds prevents known unacceptable vulnerabilities from reaching production.
explanations.d: Comments do not assess actual dependencies or images.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: A GuardDuty runtime finding identifies suspicious container behavior in EKS. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only the CloudFront distribution price class
Only the number of S3 buckets in the account
Only a generic application owner list
Affected pod, namespace, service account, image, node, and recent Kubernetes or AWS API activity

explanations.a: Price class does not describe EKS runtime behavior.
explanations.b: Bucket count does not identify the affected pod or node.
explanations.c: Ownership helps response, but technical scope needs workload-specific evidence.
explanations.d: Runtime findings need Kubernetes and AWS context to determine scope and containment steps.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.3: Scan compute resources for known vulnerabilities.
questions.text: An Inspector finding remains open after a package update. What should be verified?

answers.text: The updated artifact is rebuilt, rescanned, deployed, and the old vulnerable runtime is replaced
Only the ticket status changed to resolved
Only the vulnerability title was renamed
Only the dashboard refreshed

explanations.a: Fixing source or image contents does not remediate exposure until the updated artifact is running and validated.
explanations.b: Ticket closure does not prove the vulnerable runtime changed.
explanations.c: Renaming a finding does not remediate the vulnerable package.
explanations.d: Dashboard refresh does not force rescanning or redeployment.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: An organization must patch EC2 instances across accounts during approved maintenance windows. Which service combination fits?

answers.text: Manual SSH patching by each application team
Systems Manager Patch Manager with maintenance windows and compliance reporting
CloudFront response headers policies
AWS Certificate Manager renewal only

explanations.a: Manual patching is inconsistent and difficult to validate at scale.
explanations.b: Patch Manager automates patch deployment, and maintenance windows control timing with compliance visibility.
explanations.c: Response headers do not update operating system packages.
explanations.d: Certificate renewal does not patch compute resources.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: A critical vulnerability is found in a container base image. What update process should be used?

answers.text: Patch the ECR tag description only
SSH into each running container and install packages permanently
Rebuild affected images from patched bases, rescan, redeploy workloads, and verify no vulnerable images remain running
Suppress the vulnerability finding without a compensating control

explanations.a: Descriptions do not change image packages.
explanations.b: Manual container mutation is not repeatable and is lost on replacement.
explanations.c: Container patching requires replacing immutable image artifacts and running tasks, not patching only the registry metadata.
explanations.d: Suppression hides risk rather than remediating it.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: A patch deployment caused failures on a subset of EC2 instances. What continuous validation should have existed?

answers.text: Apply every patch to every instance at once with no checks
Delete patch logs to reduce noise
Disable health checks during patch windows
Canary patching, health checks, rollback or snapshot strategy, and post-patch compliance verification

explanations.a: All-at-once patching increases blast radius.
explanations.b: Patch logs are needed for troubleshooting and compliance.
explanations.c: Health checks help identify patch-related failures.
explanations.d: Patch automation needs staged rollout and validation so failures are detected before broad impact.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: An Amazon Inspector finding reports a vulnerable package on EC2 after the patch window completed. What should be checked?

answers.text: Patch baseline approval, instance patch state, reboot requirement, and Inspector rescan timing
Only the instance Name tag capitalization
Only the S3 bucket versioning status
Only the ALB listener priority

explanations.a: A finding can remain when the patch was not approved, not applied, not activated by reboot, or not yet rescanned.
explanations.b: Tag capitalization does not determine package patch state.
explanations.c: Bucket versioning does not patch EC2 packages.
explanations.d: Listener priority does not affect vulnerability remediation.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: A serverless workload uses dependencies packaged with Lambda functions. How should patching be handled?

answers.text: Run yum update inside the managed Lambda runtime during every invocation
Update dependencies in source or layers, rebuild packages, scan, and deploy new function versions
Wait for S3 lifecycle rules to patch the deployment ZIP
Change only the function description

explanations.a: Lambda packages are not patched by mutating the managed runtime at invocation time.
explanations.b: Lambda dependencies are patched by rebuilding and redeploying artifacts that contain updated packages.
explanations.c: Lifecycle policies do not update package dependencies.
explanations.d: Descriptions do not change deployed dependencies.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: A security team wants to prove patch compliance across accounts. What evidence should be collected?

answers.text: Only user reports that systems feel faster
Only a list of all EC2 key pairs
Systems Manager compliance results, Inspector findings, patch baselines, and maintenance window execution history
Only cost allocation tags

explanations.a: User perception does not prove patch compliance.
explanations.b: Key pairs do not show patch status.
explanations.c: Compliance evidence should show policy, execution, and remaining vulnerability state.
explanations.d: Cost tags do not validate patch application.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.4: Deploy patches across compute resources to maintain secure and compliant environments by automating update processes and by integrating continuous validation.
questions.text: A workload cannot be patched immediately because of vendor constraints. What should the security response include?

answers.text: Ignore the vulnerability permanently
Disable vulnerability scanning for the account
Publicly expose the workload so users can test it
Documented exception, compensating controls, risk owner, expiration date, and monitoring

explanations.a: Permanent ignorance leaves unmanaged risk.
explanations.b: Removing scans hides other issues and does not reduce risk.
explanations.c: Public exposure increases risk while a vulnerability remains.
explanations.d: Patch exceptions must be controlled and temporary with risk acceptance and layered protection.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: A company wants administrators to access EC2 instances in private subnets without opening inbound SSH. Which service should be used?

answers.text: Systems Manager Session Manager
Public SSH from 0.0.0.0/0
S3 static website hosting
AWS WAF managed rules

explanations.a: Session Manager provides audited administrative access without inbound SSH or bastion hosts.
explanations.b: Broad public SSH exposure increases attack surface.
explanations.c: Static website hosting does not provide shell access to instances.
explanations.d: WAF protects web requests and does not provide host administration access.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: An EC2 instance uses Session Manager but sessions fail. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the CloudFront distribution cache policy
SSM Agent status, instance profile permissions, and connectivity to Systems Manager endpoints
Only the instance key pair name
Only the RDS parameter group

explanations.a: Cache policy does not control Session Manager.
explanations.b: Session Manager requires a working agent, authorized instance role, and network path to Systems Manager services.
explanations.c: Session Manager does not depend on SSH key pairs for session establishment.
explanations.d: Database parameters do not authorize host sessions.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: A team requires browser-based temporary SSH connectivity with IAM authorization to selected EC2 instances. Which feature can help?

answers.text: AWS Backup Vault Lock
Amazon Macie
EC2 Instance Connect
AWS CodeArtifact

explanations.a: Vault Lock protects backups and does not provide administrative access.
explanations.b: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and does not create SSH sessions.
explanations.c: EC2 Instance Connect supports temporary SSH public key delivery authorized through IAM for EC2 access.
explanations.d: CodeArtifact stores packages and does not administer EC2 instances.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: A security policy requires recording administrative commands during interactive sessions. Which access path supports this better than unmanaged SSH?

answers.text: Direct SSH with no centralized logging
A shared root password for all administrators
Instance console screenshots only
Session Manager with session logging to CloudWatch Logs or S3

explanations.a: Unmanaged SSH provides weaker centralized audit evidence.
explanations.b: Shared credentials remove individual accountability.
explanations.c: Screenshots do not provide complete session command history.
explanations.d: Session Manager can record session activity to controlled log destinations for audit.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: An EKS administrator needs cluster access through IAM-authenticated identities. What should be governed?

answers.text: Cluster access mappings or authentication configuration, RBAC bindings, and CloudTrail or Kubernetes audit logs
Only the color of the kubeconfig file
A public node security group for all admin ports
A container image tag named admin

explanations.a: Secure Kubernetes administration requires identity mapping, authorization, and audit evidence.
explanations.b: File appearance does not authorize or audit cluster access.
explanations.c: Opening nodes broadly is unnecessary and risky for cluster administration.
explanations.d: Image tags do not grant Kubernetes administrative permissions.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: A bastion host is currently used for administration and is exposed to the internet. What improvement reduces risk?

answers.text: Allow SSH from every IP so responders are never blocked
Replace or restrict the bastion with Session Manager, MFA-protected access, and no broad inbound SSH
Store bastion private keys in a public bucket
Disable audit logging on the bastion

explanations.a: Broad SSH access increases brute-force and exploitation risk.
explanations.b: Managed access and narrow inbound exposure reduce the attack surface of administrative entry points.
explanations.c: Public key material storage would compromise administrative access.
explanations.d: Administrative access requires stronger audit, not less.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.5: Configure secure administrative access to compute resources.
questions.text: A production instance must not allow administrators to copy files out during sessions without approval. What should be considered?

answers.text: Unrestricted SCP and SFTP from any administrator laptop
No logging because administrators are trusted
Session Manager controls, IAM permissions, logging, and data egress restrictions aligned to the approval process
A wider inbound security group rule

explanations.a: Unrestricted file transfer can bypass data handling controls.
explanations.b: Trusted access still needs audit for compliance and investigation.
explanations.c: Administrative access design should include not just login but also what actions can be performed and audited.
explanations.d: Broader network access does not enforce file transfer approval.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A development pipeline must detect insecure code patterns before deployment. Which tool can help identify security issues in code?

answers.text: Amazon EFS Lifecycle policies
AWS Certificate Manager
Route 53 health checks
Amazon CodeGuru Security

explanations.a: EFS lifecycle policies manage file storage class and do not review code.
explanations.b: ACM manages certificates and does not analyze source code.
explanations.c: Health checks monitor endpoint availability and not code vulnerabilities.
explanations.d: CodeGuru Security can analyze code for security vulnerabilities during development workflows.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A developer wants guidance while writing code in the IDE to avoid common security defects. Which service is relevant?

answers.text: Amazon Q Developer
AWS Backup
AWS Shield Advanced
Amazon SQS

explanations.a: Amazon Q Developer can provide development assistance, including security-focused recommendations in coding workflows.
explanations.b: Backup protects data recovery points and does not provide IDE coding guidance.
explanations.c: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS and does not review source code in the IDE.
explanations.d: SQS queues messages and does not provide code security assistance.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A pipeline scans dependencies and finds a critical issue. What remediation workflow is appropriate?

answers.text: Ignore the issue because it was found before production
Fail the security gate, create a tracked finding, update the dependency, rescan, and redeploy
Deploy first and create a ticket next quarter
Delete scan results to reduce build noise

explanations.a: Preproduction findings are valuable because they can prevent exposure.
explanations.b: Pipeline remediation should stop promotion, track ownership, fix the vulnerable component, and validate the result.
explanations.c: Delayed remediation can release vulnerable code.
explanations.d: Scan evidence supports remediation and audit.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A team wants to prevent secrets from entering repositories. What pipeline control should be implemented?

answers.text: Rely only on monthly manual repository searches
Print detected secrets in build logs for confirmation
Secret scanning with failure or quarantine workflows before merge or deployment
Disable source control reviews for security branches

explanations.a: Manual monthly searches are delayed and inconsistent.
explanations.b: Build logs should not expose credential values.
explanations.c: Secret detection in the pipeline reduces the chance that credentials are stored in source or artifacts.
explanations.d: Skipping review weakens secure development workflow.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A container build should include both vulnerability scanning and policy checks for Dockerfile practices. What is the right approach?

answers.text: Use only a final production smoke test
Allow images to bypass scanning if deployment is urgent
Use only repository branch naming for security assurance
Run image scanning and policy-as-code checks as separate pipeline stages before promotion

explanations.a: Runtime smoke tests do not identify image package vulnerabilities or Dockerfile policy violations.
explanations.b: Urgency does not remove the need for compensating security review.
explanations.c: Branch naming does not validate image security.
explanations.d: Vulnerability and configuration policy checks cover different risks and should both gate release where required.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: An IaC pipeline creates public security group rules accidentally. Which security tool integration helps prevent this?

answers.text: Policy-as-code or template scanning with a gate before deployment
Post-deployment manual review only after a breach
A runtime CPU alarm
Changing instance family sizes

explanations.a: Pre-deployment IaC checks can detect network exposure before resources are created.
explanations.b: Late manual review allows risky resources to exist.
explanations.c: CPU alarms do not detect public security group rules.
explanations.d: Instance sizing does not validate IaC network exposure.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.6: Configure security tools to discover and remediate vulnerabilities within a pipeline.
questions.text: A security scan blocks a pipeline but developers cannot understand the finding. What should improve the workflow?

answers.text: Return only a generic failed message with no details
Provide finding context, severity, affected file or package, remediation guidance, and exception process
Automatically approve all exceptions with no owner
Hide scan output from the team that owns the code

explanations.a: Lack of context slows remediation and encourages unsafe bypass.
explanations.b: Actionable pipeline findings help developers fix issues without bypassing security gates.
explanations.c: Uncontrolled exceptions weaken pipeline security.
explanations.d: Owners need details to remediate vulnerabilities.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A GenAI chatbot must prevent prompt injection from causing unauthorized data disclosure. Which guardrail strategy is appropriate?

answers.text: Trust all user prompts because the model is managed
Place database credentials in the system prompt
Combine input validation, context separation, retrieval filtering, model guardrails, and output checks
Disable logging and monitoring for model interactions

explanations.a: Managed model access does not eliminate application-level prompt injection risk.
explanations.b: Secrets in prompts can be exposed or misused.
explanations.c: GenAI applications need layered controls because prompt injection can target instructions, retrieved data, and responses.
explanations.d: Monitoring is needed to detect abuse and unsafe outputs.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A Bedrock application retrieves internal documents. Users should see only documents they are authorized to access. What control is required?

answers.text: Authorize only after the model has generated the response
Index all documents as public to simplify retrieval
Use a larger model as the only access-control mechanism
Enforce authorization before retrieval and preserve user context in the retrieval layer

explanations.a: Post-generation checks can be too late if unauthorized context was already provided to the model.
explanations.b: Public indexing can expose confidential information.
explanations.c: Model size does not enforce document-level authorization.
explanations.d: RAG security depends on filtering source data by the user's permissions before content reaches the model context.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A GenAI application stores prompts and responses for quality review. What security control is needed?

answers.text: Redaction or minimization of sensitive data with retention and access controls
Store all prompts publicly for transparency
Disable all retention limits
Use object names as the only data protection control

explanations.a: Prompt and response logs can contain confidential data and must be governed like sensitive telemetry.
explanations.b: Public prompt storage can expose sensitive user and business data.
explanations.c: Indefinite retention increases data exposure risk.
explanations.d: Object naming does not enforce access or redaction.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A model output might include unsafe instructions or policy-violating content. Which protection should be added?

answers.text: Increase API timeout only
Output filtering or guardrails aligned to application policy
Store the output in an unencrypted public bucket
Trust users to report unsafe outputs after publication

explanations.a: Timeout changes do not evaluate output safety.
explanations.b: Output controls reduce the chance that generated content violates safety or business rules.
explanations.c: Public storage increases exposure and does not filter content.
explanations.d: User reports are reactive and do not enforce preventive guardrails.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A GenAI agent can invoke tools that modify AWS resources. What guardrail is most important?

answers.text: Give the agent AdministratorAccess to reduce friction
Let the model create arbitrary IAM policies at runtime
Least-privilege tool permissions, explicit action approval, and constrained tool schemas
Hide all tool calls from audit logs

explanations.a: Broad permissions create high blast radius if prompts or tools are abused.
explanations.b: Unbounded policy generation can create privilege escalation paths.
explanations.c: Agents with tool access need strict authorization and controlled actions because model output can drive real changes.
explanations.d: Tool use must be auditable for investigation and compliance.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A prompt injection attempt tries to override system instructions. What design reduces risk?

answers.text: Concatenate user content directly into privileged instructions
Disable all application-side validation
Store all system prompts in client-side code
Keep system instructions separate from user content and test prompt-injection scenarios

explanations.a: Mixing user content with trusted instructions increases injection risk.
explanations.b: Validation is needed alongside model controls.
explanations.c: Client-visible prompts can be copied and targeted by attackers.
explanations.d: Separating instruction sources and testing known attack patterns helps prevent user content from becoming trusted instructions.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.2.7: Implement protections and guardrails for generative AI applications.
questions.text: A GenAI application uses plugins that call external URLs. What should be controlled?

answers.text: Allowed destinations, request validation, secret handling, and monitoring for data exfiltration
Allow arbitrary outbound requests with all user context attached
Put API keys in the generated response for debugging
Disable network logs because plugin traffic is expected

explanations.a: External tool use can leak data or trigger unwanted actions, so egress and input/output controls are needed.
explanations.b: Unrestricted egress with full context increases exfiltration risk.
explanations.c: API keys must not be exposed in model outputs.
explanations.d: Expected traffic still needs monitoring for abuse or exfiltration.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: A private EC2 instance cannot reach an S3 VPC endpoint. Security groups allow HTTPS. What network control should be checked next?

answers.text: Only the EC2 key pair name
Route table entries and endpoint policy for the S3 gateway or interface endpoint
Only the instance Name tag
Only the CloudFront distribution cache policy

explanations.a: Key pairs do not control S3 endpoint routing.
explanations.b: S3 endpoint access depends on routing and endpoint policy in addition to security group rules where applicable.
explanations.c: Tags do not create a path to the endpoint.
explanations.d: CloudFront cache settings do not affect private S3 endpoint reachability.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: A web tier security group allows inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The application should be reachable only through CloudFront. What should change?

answers.text: Add TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 for troubleshooting
Use a wider CIDR for HTTPS
Restrict origin access to trusted CloudFront paths or source controls and remove direct broad internet access
Remove all logging to hide direct traffic

explanations.a: Opening SSH increases exposure and does not enforce CloudFront-only access.
explanations.b: A wider allow rule makes direct origin access easier.
explanations.c: Origin network controls should prevent bypass of the intended edge layer.
explanations.d: Logging should reveal bypass attempts rather than conceal them.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: A stateless network ACL denies ephemeral response ports for outbound HTTPS requests. What symptom is likely?

answers.text: IAM users automatically lose passwords
KMS keys stop rotating
S3 buckets become public
Outbound connections can fail because return traffic is blocked

explanations.a: NACL rules do not affect IAM passwords.
explanations.b: NACLs do not control KMS key rotation.
explanations.c: NACL response ports do not modify S3 bucket policies.
explanations.d: Network ACLs are stateless, so both request and response traffic must be allowed.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: A team needs layer 7 domain filtering for outbound traffic from private subnets. Which control is appropriate?

answers.text: AWS Network Firewall with domain or TLS-aware rule strategy where applicable
Security groups alone with domain names in rules
IAM policy conditions on EC2 CPU
S3 Object Lock

explanations.a: Network Firewall can enforce centrally managed traffic inspection and domain-aware egress policies.
explanations.b: Security groups do not use domain names as rule targets.
explanations.c: IAM conditions do not inspect outbound network destinations.
explanations.d: Object Lock protects retention and does not filter egress traffic.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: An application security group references a database security group incorrectly, causing connectivity failure. What should be fixed?

answers.text: Allow database access from every IP on the internet
Use the application security group as the source in the database security group inbound rule
Add an outbound WAF rule to the database
Change the database backup window

explanations.a: Broad database exposure is unsafe and unnecessary.
explanations.b: Security group referencing should allow database access from the actual application group that initiates connections.
explanations.c: WAF does not control database security group source references.
explanations.d: Backup timing does not fix connectivity authorization.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: Traffic is unexpectedly allowed between two subnets despite security group restrictions. What should be investigated?

answers.text: Only the last CloudFormation template comment
Only the number of EBS snapshots
Other security group rules, network ACLs, routing, peering or transit paths, and resource attachments
Only CloudWatch dashboard layout

explanations.a: Comments do not determine live network reachability.
explanations.b: Snapshot count does not explain permitted traffic.
explanations.c: Network authorization can involve multiple attached controls and paths, so the effective route and rule set must be reviewed.
explanations.d: Dashboard layout does not permit network paths.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.1: Design and troubleshoot appropriate network controls to permit or prevent network traffic as required.
questions.text: A Network Firewall rule update blocks legitimate application traffic. What troubleshooting approach is best?

answers.text: Delete all firewall policies immediately
Assume security groups are always the only cause
Change IAM password policy first
Review firewall logs, rule order, stateful rule behavior, and affected source-destination-port tuples

explanations.a: Removing all policies can expose the network unnecessarily.
explanations.b: Network Firewall can independently block traffic even when security groups allow it.
explanations.c: Password policy does not explain packet filtering behavior.
explanations.d: Firewall troubleshooting depends on observed drops and the exact rule evaluation path.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A company needs encrypted connectivity from an on-premises data center to a VPC over the internet. Which service fits?

answers.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Direct Connect without any encryption consideration
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
IAM Identity Center

explanations.a: Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted IPsec tunnels between on-premises networks and AWS.
explanations.b: Direct Connect is private connectivity but does not by itself provide IPsec encryption over the internet.
explanations.c: Transfer Acceleration improves S3 data transfer and does not connect networks.
explanations.d: Identity Center manages workforce access and does not create network tunnels.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A financial firm uses Direct Connect and requires encryption at layer 2 where supported. Which capability should be considered?

answers.text: S3 CORS rules
MAC Security (MACsec) on supported Direct Connect connections
AWS WAF managed rule groups
Lambda environment variables

explanations.a: CORS controls browser access to S3 and does not encrypt Direct Connect links.
explanations.b: MACsec can provide layer 2 encryption for supported Direct Connect dedicated connections.
explanations.c: WAF filters HTTP requests and does not encrypt Direct Connect frames.
explanations.d: Environment variables do not encrypt hybrid network links.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A multi-cloud environment connects to AWS through a transit hub. What security design is important?

answers.text: Use one flat route table for every environment
Disable all route propagation review
Segment routing domains and inspect traffic through approved security controls
Publish all private routes publicly

explanations.a: Flat routing increases lateral movement risk.
explanations.b: Unreviewed propagation can create unintended paths.
explanations.c: Hybrid and multi-cloud connectivity should limit lateral movement and apply inspection to sensitive paths.
explanations.d: Public route disclosure does not secure connectivity.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A Site-to-Site VPN tunnel is up but traffic does not pass to private subnets. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the ACM certificate on a public ALB
Only the S3 bucket lifecycle rule
Only the IAM role path of a Lambda function
Customer gateway routes, VPC route tables, security groups, network ACLs, and tunnel selectors

explanations.a: A public ALB certificate does not determine private VPN routing.
explanations.b: Lifecycle rules do not route VPN traffic.
explanations.c: Lambda role paths do not control VPN packet flow.
explanations.d: VPN connectivity requires both tunnel health and matching routes and controls for the traffic path.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A Direct Connect connection must fail over to VPN during disruption. What design should be used?

answers.text: Redundant connectivity with routing preference and tested failover
A single Direct Connect link with no backup
Manual route changes from memory during every outage
A larger S3 bucket for route tables

explanations.a: Hybrid connectivity resilience needs alternate paths and routing behavior validated before outages.
explanations.b: A single link creates a connectivity failure point.
explanations.c: Manual untested failover risks missing recovery objectives.
explanations.d: S3 storage size does not provide network failover.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
questions.text: A hybrid architecture needs private access to AWS services without sending traffic through the public internet. Which design helps?

answers.text: Use public endpoints with unrestricted egress for every workload
Use VPC endpoints and private routing over VPN or Direct Connect as appropriate
Disable DNS resolution for AWS services
Use IAM user passwords to encrypt network paths

explanations.a: Unrestricted public egress can violate private connectivity requirements.
explanations.b: Private access patterns keep service traffic on private network paths when the architecture requires it.
explanations.c: Private endpoint access usually depends on correct DNS resolution.
explanations.d: Passwords do not create private service connectivity.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.2: Design secure connectivity between hybrid and multi-cloud networks.
