questions.text: A partner network requires access to one internal application but not the full VPC. What secure connectivity pattern is preferable?

answers.text: Peer the full VPC with all routes propagated by default
Share all subnet route tables with the partner
Expose only the required service through PrivateLink or tightly scoped connectivity
Publish database subnets on the internet for simplicity

explanations.a: Full peering can expose more resources than required.
explanations.b: Route-table sharing does not provide least-privilege service access.
explanations.c: Service-scoped connectivity limits partner reachability and reduces lateral movement risk.
explanations.d: Public database exposure is not secure partner connectivity.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: Employees need access to a private web application without joining the corporate VPN. Which service can enforce identity-aware access?

answers.text: Public ALB with no authentication
S3 Object Lock
ECR scan-on-push
AWS Verified Access

explanations.a: Unauthenticated public access does not meet identity-aware access requirements.
explanations.b: Object Lock protects retained objects and does not authorize user access to private apps.
explanations.c: Image scanning does not provide user access control to applications.
explanations.d: Verified Access evaluates identity and device context before allowing access to private applications.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: A hybrid application requires on-premises systems to call an internal API in AWS. What must be defined?

answers.text: Network path, DNS resolution, authentication, authorization, and encryption requirements
Only the API display name
Only the number of subnets in the VPC
Only the developer who wrote the API

explanations.a: Specifically, Hybrid workload communication security depends on reachability and identity controls working together.
explanations.b: A name does not define routing, identity, or encryption.
explanations.c: Subnet count does not establish secure hybrid communication.
explanations.d: Author identity does not define runtime access requirements.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: A private application behind Verified Access is unreachable for approved users. What should be troubleshot?

answers.text: Only the S3 lifecycle policy for logs
Verified Access policy, trust provider signals, application endpoint connectivity, and DNS
Only the EC2 AMI name
Only CloudFront response headers

explanations.a: Lifecycle policy does not evaluate user access to the application.
explanations.b: Verified Access depends on policy evaluation and a working path from the service to the application endpoint.
explanations.c: AMI name alone does not explain policy or endpoint reachability.
explanations.d: Response headers do not authorize Verified Access sessions.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: A partner must access an AWS-hosted service from on-premises over private connectivity. Which requirement should be avoided?

answers.text: Strong authentication for the partner connection
Encryption over the connection where required
Broad network access to every subnet when only one service is needed
Logging of connection attempts and application access

explanations.a: Authentication helps secure hybrid communication.
explanations.b: Encryption protects data in transit.
explanations.c: Hybrid access should be scoped to the application or service to reduce lateral movement risk.
explanations.d: Logging supports investigation and governance.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: A hybrid workload uses DNS names for AWS private endpoints. What configuration is critical?

answers.text: A public bucket policy on every endpoint
A Lambda layer for every DNS query
An EC2 key pair shared with all users
Correct private DNS resolution across on-premises and AWS networks

explanations.a: Endpoint connectivity does not require public bucket policies.
explanations.b: Lambda layers do not provide hybrid DNS resolution.
explanations.c: Key pairs do not resolve endpoint names.
explanations.d: Private endpoint connectivity often fails when DNS does not resolve to the intended private addresses.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.3: Determine and configure security workload requirements for communication between hybrid environments and AWS.
questions.text: A workload requires device posture checks before user access from hybrid networks. What service pairing is relevant?

answers.text: Verified Access integrated with identity and device trust providers
Network ACLs alone
KMS key rotation alone
S3 replication rules alone

explanations.a: Device posture and identity-aware access decisions require trust provider signals tied to access policy.
explanations.b: Network ACLs do not evaluate user identity or device posture.
explanations.c: Key rotation does not authorize user-device access.
explanations.d: Replication does not evaluate hybrid user access.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: A three-tier application must isolate web, application, and database tiers. Which segmentation design is appropriate?

answers.text: Place every tier in one public subnet with broad access
Separate subnets and security groups with only required tier-to-tier flows
Use one unrestricted security group for all tiers
Rely only on instance names to separate tiers

explanations.a: Flat public placement increases exposure and lateral movement.
explanations.b: Tier segmentation limits lateral movement and exposes only the paths needed for application function.
explanations.c: A shared unrestricted group defeats tier isolation.
explanations.d: Names do not enforce network segmentation.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: An organization wants to inspect north-south traffic entering VPCs. What architecture can support this?

answers.text: Only local host files on each instance
Only IAM group membership
Centralized ingress or inspection VPC pattern using AWS Network Firewall or gateway controls
Only S3 lifecycle transitions

explanations.a: Host files do not create centralized traffic inspection.
explanations.b: IAM groups authorize identities and do not inspect network traffic.
explanations.c: North-south protection focuses on traffic entering or leaving environments through controlled inspection points.
explanations.d: Lifecycle settings do not inspect ingress or egress traffic.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: East-west traffic between application services must be restricted to approved protocols. Which control combination fits?

answers.text: Allow all internal traffic because it stays inside AWS
Use public IP addresses between every internal service
Remove all logs from internal traffic paths
Security groups, network segmentation, and inspection where required for service-to-service paths

explanations.a: Internal traffic can still be abused during lateral movement.
explanations.b: Public routing increases exposure and is unnecessary for internal segmentation.
explanations.c: Internal traffic visibility is important for detecting lateral movement.
explanations.d: East-west controls limit lateral movement between internal workloads and enforce expected protocols.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: A development VPC should not route to production database subnets. What segmentation method should be applied?

answers.text: Separate route tables and security controls that prevent development-to-production database paths
A shared route table with full propagation everywhere
A database tag named production only
One public NAT gateway as the database control

explanations.a: Route and security segmentation can enforce environment boundaries between development and production.
explanations.b: Full propagation can create unintended cross-environment reachability.
explanations.c: Tags alone do not block network traffic.
explanations.d: NAT gateways do not provide database environment authorization.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: A central inspection VPC receives traffic through Transit Gateway. What segmentation risk should be managed?

answers.text: Only the display name of the transit gateway
Route table associations and propagations that could bypass inspection
Only the number of VPC CIDR blocks
Only ACM certificate renewal status

explanations.a: Names do not control routing or inspection.
explanations.b: Transit Gateway segmentation depends on route table design that forces required paths through inspection.
explanations.c: CIDR count alone does not prove traffic flows through inspection.
explanations.d: Certificate status does not determine Transit Gateway route paths.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.4: Design network segmentation based on security requirements.
questions.text: A workload processes regulated data and should not share subnets with general workloads. What design principle applies?

answers.text: Mix all workloads in one subnet and separate them by comments
Allow every workload role to connect to regulated databases
Use isolated subnets or accounts with narrowly scoped ingress, egress, and administrative paths
Use only cost allocation tags for network isolation

explanations.a: Comments do not enforce isolation.
explanations.b: Broad role connectivity undermines segmentation.
explanations.c: Sensitive workloads should have stronger segmentation boundaries that reflect regulatory and access requirements.
explanations.d: Cost tags organize billing but do not enforce network boundaries.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.5: Identify unnecessary network access.
questions.text: A security team suspects a database subnet is reachable from development accounts. Which tool can help identify this unnecessary path?

answers.text: AWS Certificate Manager
AWS Backup
Amazon SQS delay queues
Network Access Analyzer

explanations.a: ACM manages certificates and does not analyze VPC reachability.
explanations.b: Backup creates recovery points and does not detect network paths.
explanations.c: Delay queues do not analyze network access.
explanations.d: Network Access Analyzer can evaluate network paths and identify unintended reachability.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.5: Identify unnecessary network access.
questions.text: Inspector reports network reachability to an EC2 instance from the internet. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Security groups, network ACLs, route tables, public IPs, and load balancer exposure
Only application source code comments
Only KMS key rotation settings
Only S3 object tags

explanations.a: Reachability findings require checking the effective network path and controls that expose the instance.
explanations.b: Comments do not determine internet reachability.
explanations.c: Key rotation does not expose an EC2 instance to the internet.
explanations.d: Object tags do not control EC2 network paths.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.5: Identify unnecessary network access.
questions.text: A Verified Access application policy allows a broader user group than intended. What should be corrected?

answers.text: Add a public route to the application subnet
Tighten access policy conditions and trust-provider group mappings
Disable identity checks for convenience
Change only the application logo

explanations.a: Public routing can expand exposure instead of reducing user scope.
explanations.b: Verified Access authorization depends on policy and identity context that must match intended user scope.
explanations.c: Removing identity evaluation worsens unintended access.
explanations.d: Branding does not restrict access.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.5: Identify unnecessary network access.
questions.text: A security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to a database port. What should the engineer do?

answers.text: Keep the rule because the database requires a port
Change the rule description to private
Remove the broad rule and allow only approved application security groups or trusted network ranges
Add a second broad rule for redundancy

explanations.a: A required port does not require internet-wide access.
explanations.b: Descriptions do not change reachability.
explanations.c: Database access should be limited to known application paths or administrative sources.
explanations.d: Additional broad rules increase exposure.

questions.name: Infrastructure Security
questions.objective: Skill 3.3.5: Identify unnecessary network access.
questions.text: A VPC endpoint policy allows all principals to access all S3 buckets through the endpoint. What access concern exists?

answers.text: Endpoint policies cannot affect S3 access at all
The policy automatically encrypts every bucket
The policy blocks all private traffic by default
The endpoint policy does not restrict which buckets or principals can use the private path

explanations.a: Gateway endpoint policies can restrict access through the endpoint.
explanations.b: Endpoint policies authorize requests and do not encrypt buckets.
explanations.c: The described policy is broad rather than blocking.
explanations.d: Endpoint policies can enforce least-privilege private access and should be scoped to intended resources and identities.
